data.name: Kenelm
data.gender_notes: Kenelm is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Old English Ceolwulf, meaning 'war-wolf'. In Christian tradition, Saint Kenelm was an Anglo-Saxon prince who lived around the 7th century. He was known for his generosity and charitable works, and is revered as a saint in the Catholic and Anglican churches. The name Kenelm carries the meaning “Royal nobility” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Kenelm usually hope their child will grow to embody royal nobility and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes nobility, generosity, and charitable works.
data.etymology: Kenelm belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Royal nobility.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Kenelm total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

in_greek.name: Κένελμος

in_english.long_meaning: The name Kenelm has its roots in Old English, derived from 'cyne', meaning 'royal', and 'helm', meaning 'helmet' or 'protector'. Historically, it was borne by a 9th-century Bishop of Winchester. The name symbolizes strength, bravery, and spiritual protection.

data.cultural_impact: Saint Kenelm's story continues to resonate with the British people, particularly in the areas of charitable giving and generosity. His legend serves as a reminder of the importance of kindness and compassion in the face of adversity.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Kenelm carries the spiritual weight of Saint Kenelm's life of selflessness and commitment to serving others. It also symbolizes the power of faith and the transformative effect it can have on one's life.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Kenelm, meaning "youthful helper" in Old English, symbolizes the belief in the spiritual guidance and support of the divine in one's youthful endeavors. It represents faith in the Lord as a constant companion, guiding one through life's earliest challenges and experiences.

historical_references.reference: Saint Kenelm, a young prince of Mercia, was the son of King Wulfhere and Aetheldred, daughter of King Penda of Northumbria. He is said to have lived in the early eighth century. Kenelm was born in Hereford and was raised in the monastery of Evesham. According to legend, he was hidden in a cave at Evesham during a Danish invasion, where he remained for many years. Eventually, he was discovered and restored to his throne.

Another account suggests that Saint Kenelm was a 12th-century noble of Gloucestershire. He was the son of a wealthy family and was known for his generosity and piety. He is said to have lived in the late 1100s and early 1200s. According to legend, Kenelm was murdered by his stepmother and buried in the church of St. Peter and St. Paul at Northleach, where he was later venerated as a saint.
